Package org.example.controller

Class Controller

java.lang.Object
org.example.controller.Controller
All Implemented Interfaces:
IControllerMtoV, IControllerVtoM
public class Controller extends Object implements IControllerVtoM, IControllerMtoV
Controller class serving as the mediator between the JavaFX User Interface and the underlying discrete-event simulation engine in accordance with the Model-View-Controller (MVC) pattern.

Handles user interactions, updates simulation parameters, controls thread lifecycle, synchronizes visualization updates with the JavaFX Application Thread, and manages database persistence via DAO implementations.

  • Method Details

    • startSimulation

      public void startSimulation()
      Initializes and starts a new simulation run in a dedicated background thread.

      Resets customer metrics, reads configuration values from the UI (arrival paces, service times, capacities, and customer distribution weights), configures the simulation engine and visualization canvas, and launches the engine execution thread.

      Specified by:
      startSimulation in interface IControllerVtoM

    • visualiseCustomer

      public void visualiseCustomer(int id, CustomerType type, String action)
      Relays customer movement and state transitions to the visualization canvas and UI event logs.

      Ensures all visual manipulations and log appends are safely executed on the JavaFX Application Thread via Platform.runLater(Runnable).

      Specified by:
      visualiseCustomer in interface IControllerMtoV
      Parameters:
      id - The unique identifier of the customer.
      type - The CustomerType representing the customer category (e.g., DINEIN, TAKEAWAY, ONLINE).
      action - The state transition action string (e.g., "ARRIVED", "FINISHED").

    • saveSimulationResultsToDatabase

      public void saveSimulationResultsToDatabase(MyEngine engine)
      Asynchronously calculates summary metrics and persists the completed simulation run data along with detailed individual customer logs into the database.

      Runs in a separate thread to prevent database network latency from freezing the UI.

      Parameters:
      engine - The MyEngine instance containing finished customer records and station performance statistics.
